tagline: North out of Cache Valley to a geyser kept on a timer.
intro: From the Utah line US 91 runs up the north end of Cache Valley to Franklin and Preston, where Idaho 34 turns north into Gem Valley. Around Grace the valley floor lies flat on the lava flow that turned the Bear River from the Pacific into the Great Basin. The road goes east from there to Soda Springs, an Oregon Trail landmark named for its hundreds of carbonated springs, then north on Idaho 34 toward Wyoming.

The towns were settled by Latter-day Saint pioneers. At Preston they first called their town Worm Creek, until church leaders in Salt Lake City objected in 1881. A few miles northwest of town is the site of the Bear River Massacre of 1863.

moments.title: Franklin
moments.text: Mormon pioneers settled here in 1860 thinking they were in Utah, until an 1872 survey put the town a mile into Idaho, its first permanent European settlement.

moments.title: Chesterfield
moments.text: A farm town founded in 1881 and emptied by the end of the 1930s, its meetinghouse, amusement hall and tithing house still standing for guided tours.

moments.title: Soda Springs Geyser
moments.text: Drilling for a hot swimming pool in 1937, the town struck a geyser of cold carbonated water instead, which flooded downtown for weeks and now goes off by timer every hour on the hour.

practical: This is heavy snowfall country. Idaho 34 between Soda Springs and the Wyoming line may close at times in winter.
